// 01 About

Infrastructure, secured end to end

I build and secure the infrastructure organizations run on — from Windows Server and multi-forest Active Directory to Azure infrastructure, enterprise SAN, and network security layers like Sophos NGFW and Cisco Meraki. My work spans identity, messaging, virtualization, and network engineering across MSP, federal government, and higher-education environments.

I approach infrastructure the way a network or cloud engineer does: reasoning about traffic flow and TCP/IP behavior at the packet level, designing VLAN segmentation and defense-in-depth network layouts, and validating disaster recovery through real failover testing rather than just configuration. My home lab — a self-built Proxmox VE environment running Rocky Linux, a bare-metal Sophos Firewall, and segmented Cisco networking — is where I test and break things before I ever do it in production.

I'm actively growing toward Network Engineer and Cloud Engineer roles, building deliberately on this foundation toward network security architecture.

// 04 Lab

Where I test before production

Production environments aren't where you learn to break things safely — so I run a self-directed home lab that mirrors the infrastructure patterns I work with professionally, and a few I'm actively growing into.

Virtualization
Proxmox VE host running isolated VM and LXC clusters to simulate multi-tenant enterprise environments
Linux
Rocky Linux server for hands-on administration alongside Windows Server — building cross-platform depth deliberately
Network Security
Bare-metal Sophos Firewall and Cisco APs in a defense-in-depth layout with enforced VLAN segmentation
Diagnostics
Packet capture and TCP/IP, DNS, and routing analysis to reproduce and diagnose network behavior in a controlled environment
Backup / DR
Backup and restore workflow testing, mirroring the disaster recovery discipline I run in production with Veeam and Acronis
Ongoing
Actively expanding — next additions are aimed squarely at the network and cloud engineering roles I'm targeting
